More than 60-percent of land in Harney County is public land owned by the United States and administered by the Bureau of Land Management. Harney County Sheriff's Office has a staff of six law enforcement officers. http://www.co.harney.or.us/sheriff.html The Hammonds have rejected the intervention of militias and disclaimed affiliation with the Bundy family whose sons have taken up leadership roles in the occupation and given many press interviews.

The Hammonds own 12000 acres abutting Fed refuge lands, an important migratory birding area. They sought and obtained their grazing permit, which limited when they could move their cows across refuge property. In 1994:

>Federal officials and a fence-building crew were attempting to build a fence to keep the Hammonds' cattle from trespassing on the refuge. When Hammond and his son obstructed federal workers, they were taken into custody by nine federal agents, five of whom were armed. . . Hammonds claim that the cattle trail in question was a historic route that had been continuously used since 1871.[Source](http://www.hcn.org/issues/20/582)

Those charges against the Hammonds were later dropped.

Arson charges were filed based on two fires set on Federal lands in 2001 and 2006. Feds said the first fire was set to conceal the site of an illegal deer hunt, while the second fire was an unauthorized backburn. The Hammonds say they set the first fire to stop invasive plants from growing onto their [grazing fields.](http://www.oregonlive.com/pacific-northwest-news/index.ssf/2015/12/militiamen_ranchers_in_showdow.html#incart_story_package) They were convicted by a jury but had their sentences reduced below the mandatory sentencing guidelines by the [Fed judge.](http://www.oregonlive.com/pacific-northwest-news/index.ssf/2015/12/ranchers_fight_with_feds_spark.html) The Fed prosecutors appealed and the judge's more lenient sentence was vacated and the case sent back to a different judge for re-sentencing in compliance with the "mandatory" time required by the Fed statute. The Hammonds were to report to prison on Jan 4, 2016 based on the decision on remand: >At the Oct. 7 re-sentencing hearing, U.S. District Judge Ann Aiken said the ranchers cannot disregard the law in regard to setting fires on BLM property. “You don’t have the right to make decisions on public lands when they’re not yours,” she said. Aiken said she would use discretion in sentencing the Hammonds if she could, but that wasn’t a possibility given the mandatory minimums and the jury’s decision to convict them of arson. “It wasn’t a jury of people from Eugene, it wasn’t a jury of people from Portland. It was a jury of people from Pendleton — your peers,” she said. [Source](http://www.capitalpress.com/Oregon/20151007/judge-sends-oregon-ranchers-back-to-prison)

The Hammonds have paid off the separate $400,000.00 civil restitution ordered to the Fed Government.

Militia members requested the sheriff's office protect the Hammonds from being taken into custody by federal authorities. Harney County sheriff David Ward said he sympathized with the Hammonds plight, [but declined the request.](http://www.oregonlive.com/pacific-northwest-news/index.ssf/2015/12/militiamen_ranchers_in_showdow.html#incart_story_package)

The Oath Keepers, in a [statement published](https://www.oathkeepers.org/the-hammond-family-does/) to its website prior to the occupation of the Fed building, said "we cannot force ourselves or our protection on people who do not want it. Dwight and Steven Hammond have made it clear, through their attorney, that they just want to turn themselves in and serve out their sentence. And that clear statement of their intent should be the end of the discussion on this."
